subproblems.title: Simon 6.3.2(3): on open sets the mass of an integer multiplicity current equals its weight measure
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for every open W ⊆ U, M_W(T) = μ_R(W), where M_W(T) = T.massOn W is Simon's mass 6.2.5 with the Euclidean coefficient norm (the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y) and μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M = R.measure; both sides are taken in [0, ∞].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → R.Represents T → T.massOn W = R.measure W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dtc_mass_eq_measure (DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.mass_eq_measure-a1, status accepted, candidate bff81d31ecb43002d1bfc77f510d3463c6be155f), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. It is the inherited dependency M that step 1 of the selected node's supplied proof cites; the selected proof itself gives no argument for it. The numbered proof below is that node's accepted natural-language proof, copied with one wording change: "the parent proof" is renamed to the proof of root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1. The accepted Lean candidate has the same structure: the upper bound, a lower bound on compact K ⊆ W, then exhaustion of W. In the compact lower bound (step 4) it replaces Lusin + Tietze by an L¹(μ⌞K₁)-approximation of 1_K·α_ξ by a continuous compactly supported covector field, followed by the same radial truncation, smoothing and cutoff.
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–766, stated there without proof) together with 2.4–2.8 (lines 222–283); this is the identity "M_W(S) = μ_S(W) for open W" quoted at the start of the proof of root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1. Notation: for α ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (Covector), |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing I : {1,…,n} → {1,…,P}; e^I ∈ Λⁿ is the covector e^I(v₁,…,vₙ) = det(⟨e_{I(a)}, v_b⟩)_{a,b}; μ := μ_R, so μ(B) = ∫_{M∩B} θ dHⁿ for Borel B. By definition M_W(T) = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(y)| ≤ 1 ∀y} ("admissible" forms).
1. Algebraic lemma. Let τ₁,…,τₙ ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal, σ ∈ {1, −1}, and let ζ ∈ Λₙ (MultiVector) satisfy ζ(α) = σ·α(τ₁,…,τₙ) for all α. For increasing I put d_I := det(⟨e_{I(a)}, τ_b⟩)_{a,b} = e^I(τ₁,…,τₙ). (a) Expanding each τ_b in the standard basis and using multilinearity and the alternating property (terms with a repeated basis vector vanish, the others are grouped by their increasing rearrangement with the sign of the sorting permutation) gives α(τ₁,…,τₙ) = Σ_I α(e_I)·d_I for every α. (b) By the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I d_I² = det(AᵀA), A the P×n matrix with columns τ_b; AᵀA = I_n by orthonormality, so Σ_I d_I² = 1. (c) Hence, by Cauchy–Schwarz, |ζ(α)| = |Σ_I α(e_I)d_I| ≤ |α| for every α. (d) Put α_ζ := Σ_I ζ(e^I)·e^I (a linear function of ζ). Since e^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} for increasing I, J, α_ζ(e_J) = ζ(e^J) = σd_J, hence |α_ζ| = (Σ_J d_J²)^{1/2} = 1 and ζ(α_ζ) = Σ_I ζ(e^I)² = Σ_I d_I² = 1.
2. By the field `orients` of R there is an Hⁿ-null set Z ⊆ M such that for every x ∈ M ∖ Z, ξ(x) satisfies the hypothesis of step 1 (τ an orthonormal basis of the approximate tangent space T_xM). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the function x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable on M (ξ is, ω is continuous, evaluation is continuous bilinear) and bounded by θ(x)·sup|ω|·1_{tsupport ω}(x) off Z; since tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, ∫_{M∩tsupport ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (field `locallyIntegrable_mult`). So T(ω) is the integral of an integrable function.
3. Upper bound. Let ω be admissible. For x ∈ M ∖ Z, step 1(c) and tsupport ω ⊆ W give θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) ≤ θ(x)|ω(x)| ≤ θ(x)·1_W(x). Integrating, T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ(W), so ofReal T(ω) ≤ μ(W). Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).
4. Lower bound on a compact set. Let K ⊆ W be compact and 0 < ε < 1. Fix s > 0 with K₁ := {y : dist(y, K) ≤ s} ⊆ W; K₁ is compact, K₁ ⊆ U, so μ(K₁) < ∞.
 (a) The open sets V_m := {dist(·, K) < 1/m} decrease to K and μ(K₁) < ∞, so for some m with 1/m < s the open set V := V_m satisfies K ⊆ V ⊆ K₁ and μ(V ∖ K) < ε.
 (b) Let α(y) := α_{ξ(y)} (step 1(d)); α is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, so there is a Borel map α̃ : ℝ^P → Λⁿ with α̃ = α μ-a.e. Since θ ≥ 1 on M, μ-null subsets of M are Hⁿ-null; let Z' be a Borel Hⁿ-null set containing Z ∪ ({α̃ ≠ α} ∩ M). For y ∈ M ∖ Z' we have |α̃(y)| = 1 and ξ(y)(α̃(y)) = 1. By Lusin's theorem for the finite Borel measure μ⌞K₁ on ℝ^P (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; Λⁿ is identified with ℝ^{C(P,n)} through the coefficients α(e_I)) there is a compact F₀ ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ F₀) < ε/2 and α̃|_{F₀} continuous; by inner regularity there is a compact F ⊆ (F₀ ∩ M) ∖ Z' (a Borel set, M being Borel) with μ(((F₀ ∩ M) ∖ Z') ∖ F) < ε/2. As μ(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0 and μ(Z') = 0, μ(K ∖ F) < ε; moreover F ⊆ M ∖ Z', α̃|_F is continuous, and |α̃| = 1, ξ(·)(α̃(·)) = 1 on F.
 (c) By the Tietze extension theorem (coefficientwise) α̃|_F extends to a continuous β₀ : ℝ^P → Λⁿ. Let r(v) := v / max(1, |v|), the continuous radial retraction of (Λⁿ, |·|) onto its closed unit ball, and β := r ∘ β₀. Then β is continuous, |β| ≤ 1, and β = α̃ on F (because |α̃| = 1 there).
 (d) Let φ_δ be a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, ∫φ_δ = 1, support in B_δ(0)) and β_δ := β * φ_δ (coefficientwise convolution). Then β_δ is smooth, |β_δ(y)| ≤ ∫|β(y − z)|φ_δ(z) dz ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm, Minkowski's integral inequality), and β_δ → β uniformly on compact sets as δ ↓ 0 (β is uniformly continuous on compact sets). Fix δ with |β_δ − β| ≤ ε on F.
 (e) Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(V) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and χ = 1 on K (smooth Urysohn lemma), and set ω := χβ_δ. Then ω is smooth with compact tsupport ⊆ V ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and |ω| ≤ 1: ω is admissible.
 (f) Since χ = 1 on F ⊆ K and ω = 0 off V, T(ω) = ∫_{F} θ ξ(β_δ) dHⁿ + ∫_{M∩(V∖F)} θ χ ξ(β_δ) dHⁿ. For y ∈ F (so y ∈ M ∖ Z'): ξ(y)(β_δ(y)) = ξ(y)(α̃(y)) + ξ(y)(β_δ(y) − β(y)) ≥ 1 − |β_δ(y) − β(y)| ≥ 1 − ε by step 1(c) and (b). For y ∈ (M ∩ (V ∖ F)) ∖ Z, |χ(y)ξ(y)(β_δ(y))| ≤ 1. Since μ(V ∖ F) ≤ μ(V ∖ K) + μ(K ∖ F) < 2ε, we get T(ω) ≥ (1 − ε)μ(F) − 2ε ≥ (1 − ε)(μ(K) − ε) − 2ε ≥ μ(K) − ε(μ(K) + 3).
 (g) Hence M_W(T) ≥ ofReal T(ω) ≥ μ(K) − ε(μ(K) + 3); letting ε ↓ 0 gives M_W(T) ≥ μ(K).
5. Exhaustion. W is open, so W = ⋃_m K_m with the increasing compact sets K_m := {y ∈ W : |y| ≤ m, dist(y, ℝ^P ∖ W) ≥ 1/m} (K_m := {|y| ≤ m} if W = ℝ^P). By continuity of μ from below and step 4, μ(W) = sup_m μ(K_m) ≤ M_W(T). Together with step 3, M_W(T) = μ(W) in [0, ∞].
proof_key_steps: A unit simple n-vector ζ satisfies |ζ(α)| ≤ |α|_Euclid (Cauchy–Binet) and has a dual covector α_ζ, linear in ζ, with |α_ζ| = 1 and ζ(α_ζ) = 1.
Upper bound: for every admissible ω, T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ_R(W).
Lower bound on compact K ⊆ W: Lusin, Tietze, radial retraction, mollification and a cutoff give an admissible ω with T(ω) ≥ μ_R(K) − ε(μ_R(K) + 3).
Exhaust the open set W by compact sets to conclude M_W(T) = μ_R(W).

subproblems.title: Mass on W is determined by the action on forms supported in W, across a change of domain
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, V, W ⊆ ℝ^P with V ⊆ U and W ⊆ V, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and S' ∈ 𝒟_n(V) (GeometricCurrentOn). Suppose S(ιω) = S'(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Here ι = testFormOnInclusion (V ⊆ U) regards a test form supported in V as a test form supported in U. Then M_W(S) = M_W(S'). M_W = massOn is Simon's mass 6.2.5 with the Euclidean coefficient norm: the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal(T(ω)) over test forms ω in the domain with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U V W : Set (Euclid P)) (hVU : V ⊆ U) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (S' : GeometricCurrentOn V n), W ⊆ V → (∀ ω : TestFormOn V n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W → S (testFormOnInclusion hVU n ω) = S' ω) → S.massOn W = S'.massOn W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dtc_massOn_eq_of_agreeOn (DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.mass_agree-a1, status accepted, candidate 0c79e2ab8192c141221cbe30fcd242e4becc6f00), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. The argument is the first assertion of step 1 of the selected node's supplied proof: the admissible families defining the two masses consist of the same underlying forms, and the currents agree on them. Here it is stated for a current S in U and a current S' in a subdomain V ⊆ U. This is the argument that candidate formalizes.
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.5 (chapter-06.txt lines 228–233, the mass M_W) read with the terminology 2.16 (lines 335–337: T₁ = T₂ in W).
Notation. For D ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟ⁿ(D) = TestFormOn D n is the set of smooth compactly supported n-forms ω on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ D. An element is a form together with proofs of these properties, and two elements with the same underlying form are equal (Subtype.ext). For a current T ∈ 𝒟_n(D) and a set W, A_D(W) := massAdmissibleOn D n W = {ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(D) : tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y}, where |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm. Then M_W(T) = T.massOn W = sup{ofReal(T(ω)) : ω ∈ A_D(W)} ∈ [0, ∞], the sSup of the image set. The map ι := testFormOnInclusion hVU n : 𝒟ⁿ(V) → 𝒟ⁿ(U) keeps the underlying form (testFormOnInclusion_coe). No openness is needed.
1. Put I := {ofReal(S(ω)) : ω ∈ A_U(W)} and I' := {ofReal(S'(ω')) : ω' ∈ A_V(W)}. Since M_W(S) = sup I and M_W(S') = sup I', it suffices to prove I = I'.
2. (I ⊆ I'.) Let ω ∈ A_U(W). Its underlying form is a test form and tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ V, so the same form defines an element ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V). Both conditions defining A_V(W), tsupport ⊆ W and pointwise norm ≤ 1, concern only the underlying form, so ω' ∈ A_V(W). Also ιω' and ω have the same underlying form, so ιω' = ω. The hypothesis applies to ω', because tsupport ω' = tsupport ω ⊆ W, and gives S(ω) = S(ιω') = S'(ω'). Hence ofReal(S(ω)) = ofReal(S'(ω')) ∈ I'.
3. (I' ⊆ I.) Let ω' ∈ A_V(W) and ω := ιω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). It has the same underlying form as ω', so ω ∈ A_U(W), and the hypothesis gives S(ω) = S(ιω') = S'(ω'). Hence ofReal(S'(ω')) = ofReal(S(ω)) ∈ I.
4. By steps 2 and 3, I = I', so M_W(S) = sup I = sup I' = M_W(S'). ∎
(In Lean: unfold GeometricCurrentOn.massOn, apply congr 1 and ext r, then prove the two inclusions above.)
proof_key_steps: Each mass M_W is the supremum of ofReal of the current's values on its admissible forms, i.e. those supported in W with pointwise norm ≤ 1.
Because W ⊆ V ⊆ U, the admissible forms for U and for V are the same underlying forms, related by testFormOnInclusion.
The hypothesis gives equal values on corresponding forms, so the two value sets coincide and the suprema are equal.

subproblems.title: Local finiteness of Hⁿ⌞M and of the weight of an integer multiplicity representation
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation in U (an IMRep U n). That is: M = R.carrier is Borel with M ⊆ U; θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ is Borel with θ ≥ 1 on M; and ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, where H^n = μHE[n]. Let μ_R = R.measure = θ·(H^n⌞M), i.e. (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ. Then for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ U: H^n(M ∩ K) < ∞ and μ_R(K) < ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (R.carrier ∩ K) ≠ ∞ ∧ R.measure K ≠ ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsd_imrep_compact_measure_ne_top (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.density_eq_multiplicity-a1.imrep_local_finiteness-a1, status accepted, candidate 702e7082a5a7012f7a8f6efd9d272697e426f50b), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. Its second conclusion is step 2 of the selected node's supplied proof: μ_i(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ W ⊆ U_i, by the field locallyIntegrable_mult. The first conclusion is proved alongside. This is the argument that candidate formalizes.
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Definition 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–747): the multiplicity θ is a locally Hⁿ-integrable positive integer-valued function. The frozen contract encodes this by the IMRep fields mult_pos and locallyIntegrable_mult.
Notation. Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P; M = R.carrier; θ(x) = R.mult x ∈ ℕ, viewed in [0, ∞]; μ_R = R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ. Fix a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ U. No openness of U is used.
1. K is a compact subset of the Hausdorff space ℝ^P, hence closed, hence Borel (IsCompact.measurableSet).
2. (Weight of K.) Since K is measurable, μ_R(K) = ∫_K θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) by the definition of withDensity (withDensity_apply), and (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞K = Hⁿ⌞(K ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict). Hence μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ, after commuting the intersection.
3. The field locallyIntegrable_mult, applied to the compact set K ⊆ U, gives ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ≠ ∞. By step 2, μ_R(K) ≠ ∞. This is the second conclusion.
4. (θ ≥ 1 on M.) For x ∈ M ∩ K, the field mult_pos gives 0 < R.mult x in ℕ. Hence 1 ≤ R.mult x, and after casting to [0, ∞], 1 ≤ θ(x).
5. (Measurability.) x ↦ θ(x) ∈ [0, ∞] is measurable. It is the measurable map R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ (field measurable_mult) followed by the cast ℕ → [0, ∞], and every map out of the discrete space ℕ is measurable (measurable_from_nat).
6. (Unweighted measure.) Hⁿ(M ∩ K) = ∫_{M∩K} 1 dHⁿ (setLIntegral_one). This is at most ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ by monotonicity of the set lower integral (setLIntegral_mono), using steps 4 and 5. The right side is finite by step 3, so Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≠ ∞. This is the first conclusion. ∎
proof_key_steps: A compact K is closed, hence Borel.
μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ by withDensity_apply and restrict_restrict, and this is finite by locallyIntegrable_mult.
θ ≥ 1 on M (mult_pos) gives Hⁿ(M ∩ K) = ∫_{M∩K} 1 dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞.

subproblems.title: Measures that agree on the open subsets of an open set O, one of them finite on compact subsets of O, agree on all Borel subsets of O
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let O ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let μ, ν be measures on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P (Mathlib Measure (Euclid P)). Assume that μ(C) < ∞ for every compact C ⊆ O, and that μ(G) = ν(G) for every open G ⊆ O. Then μ(A) = ν(A) for every Borel set A ⊆ O.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (O : Set (Euclid P)) (μ ν : Measure (Euclid P)), IsOpen O → (∀ C : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact C → C ⊆ O → μ C ≠ ∞) → (∀ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G → G ⊆ O → μ G = ν G) → ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → A ⊆ O → μ A = ν A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cmc_ml_measure_eq_of_eq_on_open_subsets (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.minimality_localizes-a1.measure_agree_on_borel-a1, status accepted, candidate 9adc8b20a486bc0e31782b03829041145baea564), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. The proof below is steps 3–5 of the selected node's supplied proof, stated for general measures μ, ν and an open set O: exhaust O by relatively compact open sets, apply π-system uniqueness of finite measures, and pass to the limit by continuity from below. Only μ is assumed finite on compact subsets of O; the finiteness of ν on the exhausting sets follows from ν(O_i) = μ(O_i). This is the argument that candidate formalizes.
Notation. d(x) := inf{|x − y| : y ∈ ℝ^P ∖ O} ∈ [0, ∞] is the distance from x to ℝ^P ∖ O (Mathlib infEDist x Oᶜ), with d ≡ +∞ when O = ℝ^P (the infimum over the empty set). d is continuous as a map to [0, ∞]: it is 1-Lipschitz when ℝ^P ∖ O ≠ ∅ and constant otherwise. Also d(x) = 0 for every x ∉ O.
1. (Exhaustion.) For i ∈ ℕ put O_i := {x ∈ ℝ^P : |x| < i and d(x) > 1/(i+1)}. This is the same kind of exhaustion as V_q = B_q(0) ∖ cthickening(1/q, ℝ^P ∖ W) = {|x| < q, d(x) > 1/q} in step 3 of the selected proof.
 (a) O_i is open: it is the intersection of the open sets {|x| < i} and d⁻¹((1/(i+1), ∞]), the latter open because d is continuous.
 (b) The set F_i := {x : |x| ≤ i and d(x) ≥ 1/(i+1)} is closed and contains O_i, so closure(O_i) ⊆ F_i. If x ∉ O, then d(x) = 0 < 1/(i+1), so x ∉ F_i. Hence closure(O_i) ⊆ F_i ⊆ O.
 (c) closure(O_i) is closed and contained in the closed ball of radius i about 0, hence compact (Heine–Borel).
 (d) O_i ⊆ O_j whenever i ≤ j, since then |x| < i ≤ j and 1/(j+1) ≤ 1/(i+1).
 (e) ⋃_i O_i = O. Indeed O_i ⊆ closure(O_i) ⊆ O for every i. Conversely let x ∈ O. The set ℝ^P ∖ O is closed and does not contain x, so x is not in its closure and d(x) > 0. Choose an integer m ≥ 1 with 1/m < d(x) and an integer k > |x|, and put i := max(m, k). Then |x| < k ≤ i and 1/(i+1) < 1/m < d(x), so x ∈ O_i.
2. (Finiteness.) For each i, μ(O_i) ≤ μ(closure(O_i)) < ∞ by hypothesis, because closure(O_i) is a compact subset of O by step 1(b),(c). Since O_i is an open subset of O, ν(O_i) = μ(O_i) < ∞.
3. (Uniqueness on O_i.) Fix i and let μ_i := μ⌞O_i and ν_i := ν⌞O_i, so μ_i(B) = μ(B ∩ O_i) and ν_i(B) = ν(B ∩ O_i) for Borel B. By step 2 these are finite measures. For every open G ⊆ ℝ^P, the set G ∩ O_i is open and contained in O, so μ_i(G) = μ(G ∩ O_i) = ν(G ∩ O_i) = ν_i(G). In particular μ_i(ℝ^P) = ν_i(ℝ^P) (take G = ℝ^P). The open subsets of ℝ^P are closed under finite intersections, so they form a π-system (Mathlib isPiSystem_isOpen), and they generate the Borel σ-algebra (BorelSpace.measurable_eq). Two finite measures with the same total mass that agree on a generating π-system are equal (Dynkin's π–λ uniqueness theorem; Mathlib MeasureTheory.ext_of_generate_finite). Hence μ_i = ν_i.
4. (Continuity from below.) Let A ⊆ O be a Borel set. The sets A ∩ O_i increase with i by step 1(d), and ⋃_i (A ∩ O_i) = A ∩ ⋃_i O_i = A ∩ O = A by step 1(e). By continuity of measures from below, μ(A) = sup_i μ(A ∩ O_i) = sup_i μ_i(A) and ν(A) = sup_i ν(A ∩ O_i) = sup_i ν_i(A). By step 3, μ_i(A) = ν_i(A) for every i; therefore μ(A) = ν(A). ∎
proof_key_steps: Exhaust O by the open sets O_i = {|x| < i, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ O) > 1/(i+1)}, which increase to O and have compact closures in O.
μ(O_i) ≤ μ(closure O_i) < ∞ and ν(O_i) = μ(O_i), so μ⌞O_i and ν⌞O_i are finite measures.
μ⌞O_i and ν⌞O_i agree on every open G, since G ∩ O_i is an open subset of O; this includes G = ℝ^P. The open sets form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra, so μ⌞O_i = ν⌞O_i.
For Borel A ⊆ O, continuity from below along A ∩ O_i ↑ A gives μ(A) = sup_i μ(A ∩ O_i) = sup_i ν(A ∩ O_i) = ν(A).
